name: multiple_choice: Which of the following is accurate with respect to…

request.questionText: Which of the following is accurate with respect to sampling distributions and statistical uncertainty? (1) In the context of statistical inference, uncertainty arises from randomness inherent to our sampling procedure, not as a characteristic of any one particular sample generated by that procedure. (2) The methodological tools of statistical inference are used to approximate the variability that we would observe in a summary statistic if it were feasible to sample repeatedly using the same process from the same population. (3) If sample data are generated by a random process, we may conceptualize a sampling distribution for some summary statistic estimated from the sample.
